summary:
We developed Aurora Base: 10 Days to Pioneer, an interactive browser-based mission simulator designed specifically for junior astronauts ages 7 to 12, created by team The Magics for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge "Build a Mission Simulator for Junior Astronauts".

The project addresses the educational gap in space outreach: while traditional information is often too abstract or technical for children, our simulator turns real deep-space exploration dilemmas into an intuitive, gamified 10-day survival experience on the Moon or Mars. Players strategically manage limited resources among oxygen, radiation shields, and science, leading a crew of specialists while facing real conditions powered by NASA's open data.

This project is important because it fosters early scientific vocations, making real space science accessible (integrating the DONKI and OSDR databases) and teaching new generations that every decision in space involves a critical balance between human survival and research.
details:
Here are the detailed project specifications for Aurora Base: 10 Days to Pioneer, developed by team The Magics for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, translated into English and excluding the AI assistance mention:

  • What does it do and how does it work?Aurora Base: 10 Days to Pioneer is an interactive, browser-based mission simulator designed for junior astronauts ages 7 to 12. Players take on the role of Mission Commander at an outpost on the Moon or Mars during a 10-day survival challenge while awaiting the arrival of the relief ship Pioneer. Each game day, players allocate limited energy resources across three vital systems—life support (oxygen), radiation shielding, and scientific research—while managing a four-person specialist crew (Engineer, Geologist, Medic, and Rover Pilot) and deploying them on high-risk tactical missions.
    • Translates complex astrophysics, orbital mechanics, and space weather concepts into intuitive, hands-on gameplay.
    • Encourages critical thinking, strategic resource management, and risk assessment under pressure.
    • Connects young learners directly with authentic open data from space agencies.
    • Frontend & Web Technologies: HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript engineered into a lightweight, self-contained single-file web application with custom SVG animations and responsive design.
    • Data & APIs: NASA Open APIs, specifically the Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI) and the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR).
    • Age-Appropriate Accessibility: Designed specifically for ages 7 to 12, balancing scientific accuracy with clear visual feedback, simple controls, and dual-language support.
    • System Resilience & Transparency: Built with graceful fallbacks and live connection status indicators so the simulator remains fully playable even if external APIs experience downtime, clearly distinguishing live observations from simulation modes.
    • Hackathon Compliance: Strict adherence to NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines, avoiding the use of official NASA logos or branding while keeping game units clearly labeled as simplified educational representations.
